newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine govt apologises for late T-bill payments.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine govt apologises for late T-bill payments.

text.p: A top Ukraine official issued a public apology in parliament on Friday after the finance ministry delayed Treasury bill payments for the third time in less than a month.
"I would like to apologise for the delay to those affected," deputy prime minister Viktor Pynzenyk told parliament.
Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko would apply strict controls to make sure the ministry pays in the future, he said.
"The Prime Minister will not repeat his request a second time," Pynzenyk said.
Banks were due to receive 4.12 trillion karbovanets ($23.3 million) on September 18 from the ministry, which in practice usually pays the morning after funds are due.
But this time the money, comprising principal and interest payments, did not arrive until late on September 19.

Transactions in older T-bill issues are still recorded in karbovanets, the old currency which was replaced earlier this month by the hryvnia. The hryvnia, worth 100,000 karbovanets, is currently $1.76.
Ukrainian bankers had mixed reactions to the delay.
"The problems will continue," said Serhy Matvichuk of Perkombank.
"It was a large problem yesterday, and we thought they would be three days late," said Matvichuk. "We were happy when our money came in at 4 p.m.
Matvichuk said the ministry must pay out 83 million hryvnia ($47 million) on September 25.
"There is no hope that they will be able to pay in the future," he said. "I'm pessimistic."
The T-bill market, started 18 months ago, would stop growing and foreign investors would wait rather than invest, he said.
His bank is investing only in short-term paper because of the risk of not being paid, he said.

The finance ministry has not commented on the delay, the third since late August 29 when it was half a day late in paying $23 million. On September 11 a similar delay occurred with a $22 million payment.
But Kyrylo Shevchenko of Finance and Credit Bank said the ministry would pay up on time in future for fear of losing customers.
"If delays continue there will be a loss of confidence on the T-bill market. The ministry understands this," he said.
Central bank chairman Viktor Yushchenko vowed on Thursday that delays would not be repeated, and said the problem had been raised with the prime minister and President Leonid Kuchma.
Ukraine recently clarified complex tax rules on T-bills to attract more foreign investors.
Bankers have said the finance ministry does not have the money to cover the payments, and also blamed delays on infighting between the central bank and ministry.

The central bank plans to raise 150 trillion karbovanets this year in T-bill sales to go towards covering the projected 467 trillion karbovanets budget deficit. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
